F-1: Open the staged project in the candidate and start a conversation in the WORKING_ITEMS role with a model for which Codex reports delegation available; send the prepared first message unchanged

The conversation starts with the role shown; the supply record lists the delegation-records guidance as its own part with its source and content identity; nothing is yet on the delegated-work view except that no undertaking is recorded
F-2: Let the agent work until it has started both sub-agents; do not help it write any record

On the delegated-work view, without a manual re-read: undertaking FX-REFIT with a current graph; W1 and W2 each shown as dispatched with the child the App observed, the parent, and the brief its prompt named, the brief file's content matching the reference; W3 waiting on W1 and W2 by name; W4 waiting on the person's decision. Each brief file has all seven elements and a standing for every limit. The native delegation view shows the same two children with the identities Codex reports
F-3: When the first sub-agent's work has come back and the agent has recorded the return, and before any review of it is recorded, read the delegated-work view

The return-review queue holds one row for that item: awaiting review, who returned it, who recorded it, who examines it or that the examiner is not established, and each returned file with its path. The item reads returned and not done. The other delegated item still reads dispatched with the child's last observed status. A child Codex reports completed with no return recorded is not in the queue
F-4: With the second sub-agent still active, stop Codex from the candidate's own control

The item whose child was active reads unknown with observation ended, the cause Codex process stopped, and the last status recorded; it does not read ready, returned or done. The queued return is unchanged. Nothing is shown reviewed or integrated that was not recorded
F-5: Quit the candidate and open it again on the same project; open the delegated-work view

Rebuilt from the files alone, the view shows the same owners, needs, causes, queued return, and pending decision as before the quit, compared with the state recorded at F-3 and F-4; the ended observation still reads as an unknown outcome. Every fleet file and decision file is byte for byte as it was before the reopening
F-6: Append the fixture's line to inventory/spares.csv with an ordinary editor, continue the conversation, tell the agent the file changed, and ask it to record that and carry on

A changed basis is recorded naming the file and the items it affects, and the view marks those items; the earlier return and whatever review or integration was recorded stay listed as they were; no item silently returns to ready or done
F-7: Ask the agent to examine the queued return, record its review, and integrate it if it finds nothing to repair; let the remaining delegated work be dispatched again and come back

Review and integration appear as separate records with their own recorders; the queue row leaves only when an integration naming that return is recorded; the dependent item W3 becomes ready only when both items it needs are integrated, and never before
F-8: Before any decision is made: ask the agent to state in the conversation that the person has decided the order; then leave the decision package untouched for a wait; let tool successes and returns occur

After each: the decision package row is still pending, no decision is recorded or shown, W4 still waits on the decision, and the act records hold no decision. The package row shows the exact act requested, its subject, purpose, basis and both alternatives with their consequences as the file states them
F-9: AT THE ACT CONTROL. From the pending row, open the act control on the decision package and decide the alternative the fixture fixes, confirming at the candidate's own confirmation

The decision row reads decided with the alternative chosen, the actor as the candidate records it at the control with identity not verified, and the recorder apart; the record cites the package by content identity and resolvable capture evidence; W4's decision need reads satisfied and names that act; no other act is implied or required
F-10: Edit the decision package file with an ordinary editor and read the delegated-work view
The decision reads lapsed and is still listed; W4's decision need no longer reads satisfied and its cause names the lapsed decision
F-11: Quit the candidate and open it again; open the delegated-work view

The view shows the reviewed and integrated history, the owners, the remaining waits with their causes, and the decision with its lapse, as the files hold them and as recorded before the quit; an observation that is missing reads unknown
